purpose: Choose navigation by destination structure, task and context. Defaults are starting hypotheses, not platform mandates.

families.title: SaaS and dashboard
families.default: Persistent sidebar, visible workspace identity and contextual page header. Add breadcrumbs when hierarchy warrants them.

families.title: Desktop website
families.default: Brand left, readable primary routes and distinct actions.
families.configuration: Choose header composition independently of destination hierarchy. See headerCompositions and headerRules. Preserve a common row center and an intentional shared content container.

families.title: Mobile website
families.default: Compact brand and identifiable menu trigger; include a priority action only when space and visitor readiness justify it.
alternatives: Expanding header menu with a separate contextual action bar
families.configuration: Brand and menu may align left or right, or brand may center. Keep priority actions distinct from menu controls and explain any persistent bottom bar role.

families.title: Native mobile app
families.default: Stable bottom destinations with contextual top navigation where primary destinations justify that structure.
alternatives: Top-level tabs for a shared context
Focused task stack with explicit exit
families.configuration: Treat this as a design hypothesis. Verify current target-platform conventions before implementing native controls, gestures or adaptive behavior.

principles: Distinguish global destinations, local location and task progression.
Keep stable ordering, meaningful labels, explicit current location and clear scope.
Separate destination navigation from actions; a floating bottom action bar is not a destination bar.
Distinguish structural alternatives from alignment or placement configurations.
Preserve appropriate filters, position, drafts and return context. Define consequences when preservation is impossible.
Use responsive changes to preserve hierarchy rather than merely hide destinations.
Keep navigation predictable across equivalent tasks. Marketing variety belongs mainly in content, not arbitrary navigation changes.
Verify current primary platform guidance for real native behavior; these authored heuristics are not compliance claims.

reviewDimensions.anatomy: Identity, destinations, location, utilities and actions; include only what the task needs.
reviewDimensions.behavior: Selection, expansion, dismissal, back, persistence and scroll response.
reviewDimensions.states: Active, expanded, unavailable, overflow, notifications and pending work when relevant.
reviewDimensions.access: Keyboard and focus behavior, accessible naming, non-hover operation and understandable current location.
reviewDimensions.adaptation: Long labels, narrow/wide layouts, input modalities, keyboard occlusion and platform safe areas.
reviewDimensions.measurement: Destination finding, orientation, safe switching and return success; define context and guardrails, do not invent performance gains.

patterns.title: Persistent sidebar
patterns.intent: Frequent switching among related work areas
patterns.selectWhen: Use for repeat work with a stable destination hierarchy.
patterns.default: For product UI: sidebar head with context switcher; body with navigation search, direct links and accordion link groups with optional dividers; footer with user menu. Keep content alongside the sidebar on wide layouts.
patterns.tradeoff: Icon-only rails demand recognition; deep nesting can hide work.
patterns.adaptation: Retain hierarchy in a narrow drawer; do not silently discard destinations.
patterns.evaluation: Can people find a destination and identify current workspace and location?
patterns.implementationStatus: Rendered in product demo: work-first, lifecycle and focused groupings. Search filters destinations; native disclosures operate in Inspect/Browse. Workspace switching and account operations remain bounded prototypes.
anatomy: sidebar-body: links and accordion groups, optional dividers

patterns.title: Website topbar
patterns.intent: Orient visitors and expose the main routes
patterns.selectWhen: Use when the primary information architecture is compact enough to scan.
patterns.default: Brand left, primary destinations grouped, actions visually separate.
patterns.tradeoff: Larger menus expose more routes but increase scanning and maintenance.
patterns.adaptation: Collapse before links collide; preserve grouping and priority in the mobile menu.
patterns.evaluation: Can unfamiliar visitors predict where links lead?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Mobile website menu
patterns.intent: Expose the full site hierarchy in limited space
patterns.selectWhen: Use when direct header links no longer fit.
patterns.default: Identifiable menu trigger, current context, clear close and return behavior.
patterns.tradeoff: An overlay saves space but hides routes until opened.
patterns.adaptation: Support long labels, scrolling, keyboard access and both portrait and landscape.
patterns.evaluation: Can visitors open, explore, dismiss and resume without losing their place?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Bottom destination bar
patterns.selectWhen: Use for a small set of frequently visited peer destinations.
patterns.default: Labeled destinations, explicit active location and stable order.
patterns.tradeoff: Persistent chrome occupies space; many destinations weaken clarity.
patterns.adaptation: Consider safe areas and keyboard overlap; retain destination identity when adapting.
patterns.evaluation: Can users switch and return to the expected context?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Workspace and account switcher
patterns.intent: Establish the identity and scope of work
patterns.selectWhen: Use when multiple accounts, organizations or workspaces are available.
patterns.default: Show current scope and explain consequential switching effects.
patterns.tradeoff: Fast switching can cause wrong-scope actions if identity is subtle.
patterns.adaptation: Keep current scope visible in compact layouts and allow long names.
patterns.evaluation: Can people tell where a change will apply before acting?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Search and command entry
patterns.intent: Find known destinations, objects or actions
patterns.selectWhen: Use as a shortcut alongside discoverable navigation.
patterns.default: Distinguish destination results, objects and executable actions.
patterns.tradeoff: Expert speed can conceal discoverability and action consequences.
patterns.adaptation: Provide an explicit entry point without requiring keyboard shortcuts.
patterns.evaluation: Can people distinguish navigation from execution and recover from a mistaken query?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Breadcrumbs
patterns.selectWhen: Use when ancestry helps orientation or movement to a parent.
patterns.default: Show meaningful ancestors and current location; do not imply browsing history.
patterns.tradeoff: Long trails consume space and may imply a hierarchy the product does not have.
patterns.adaptation: Keep current and useful parent context when collapsing ancestors.
patterns.evaluation: Does the trail reflect the real hierarchy and lead to expected parents?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Peer-view tabs
patterns.intent: Switch views within a shared context
patterns.selectWhen: Use when views share an object or clear parent context.
patterns.default: Clear active view, stable labels and defined persistence of work.
patterns.tradeoff: Too many tabs obscure information architecture.
patterns.adaptation: Expose overflow; retain selected view and keyboard access.
patterns.evaluation: Can users predict what changes and what context remains?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Local navigation
patterns.selectWhen: Use for documentation, settings or complex subsections.
patterns.default: Keep subsection identity and current item clear.
patterns.tradeoff: Multiple navigation columns can compete for attention.
patterns.adaptation: Move local routes to a contextual menu while keeping global scope distinct.
patterns.evaluation: Can people distinguish global destinations from local content?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Section navigation
patterns.intent: Move within a long document or page
patterns.selectWhen: Use when readers benefit from direct access to meaningful sections.
patterns.default: Human-readable anchors with an identifiable current section where useful.
patterns.tradeoff: Sticky chrome costs reading space; inaccurate active tracking can mislead.
patterns.adaptation: Use a compact select or disclosure when the list dominates the viewport.
patterns.evaluation: Can readers reach a section and retain context without headings being obscured?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Back and return
patterns.intent: Return to the expected previous context
patterns.selectWhen: Use for nested records, flows and narrow master-detail layouts.
patterns.default: Distinguish parent navigation, history back and cancel; preserve relevant work context.
patterns.tradeoff: An ambiguous back action can discard work or return somewhere unexpected.
patterns.adaptation: Follow researched host-platform conventions when implementing actual native behavior.
patterns.evaluation: Are filters, position and unfinished work preserved or explicitly resolved?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Master-detail navigation
patterns.intent: Inspect records while retaining collection context
patterns.selectWhen: Use for repeated scanning and opening of items.
patterns.default: Retain selection and collection scope while showing the record.
patterns.tradeoff: Split panes reduce detail space and can complicate bulk selection.
patterns.adaptation: Use successive views on narrow layouts with a reliable return path.
patterns.evaluation: Can people inspect several records without repeatedly rebuilding context?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Guided steps
patterns.intent: Complete dependent stages with clear progress
patterns.selectWhen: Use where prerequisites or consequences justify staged work.
patterns.default: Name meaningful stages and explain revisiting, validation and saved progress.
patterns.tradeoff: A rigid flow can slow experts and conceal dependencies.
patterns.adaptation: Keep current stage and progress understandable without squeezing all labels.
patterns.evaluation: Can users complete, correct and resume the flow?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Sequential traversal
patterns.intent: Move through ordered reading or review
patterns.selectWhen: Use when sequence matters or people process a scoped set.
patterns.default: Identify adjacent item or stage and preserve position in the set.
patterns.tradeoff: Sequential controls may obscure direct access to another item.
patterns.adaptation: Keep target labels usable and avoid collision with persistent action controls.
patterns.evaluation: Can people predict the next item and return without losing context?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Contextual task action bar
patterns.intent: Complete or modify the current task
patterns.selectWhen: Use for save, continue, submit or approval actions with a clear scope.
patterns.default: Separate primary action, secondary choices and cancellation; show pending work.
patterns.tradeoff: Persistent actions can obscure content and suggest readiness prematurely.
patterns.adaptation: Account for virtual keyboards, safe areas and content clearance.
patterns.evaluation: Can people understand scope, readiness and consequences before acting?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Focused task navigation
patterns.selectWhen: Use when reducing unrelated navigation helps a consequential task.
patterns.default: Retain identity, progress and explicit exit with recovery.
patterns.tradeoff: Reduced navigation may feel trapping without a clear exit.
patterns.adaptation: Preserve draft and return semantics through interruption or viewport changes.
patterns.evaluation: Can users finish, defer or leave safely?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

patterns.title: Collection traversal
patterns.intent: Explore a bounded or growing result set
patterns.selectWhen: Use when a collection exceeds one practical view.
patterns.default: Keep scope, loaded count and return position understandable.
variants: Continuous loading with explicit end and recovery
patterns.tradeoff: Continuous loading complicates locating items and reaching content after the list.
patterns.adaptation: Preserve filters and position; ensure loading controls remain reachable.
patterns.evaluation: Can people find an item, revisit it and understand the extent of results?
patterns.implementationStatus: Authoring guidance; no dedicated interactive renderer guaranteed

headerCompositions.structure: [Identity + destinations (+ search when justified)] [flexible space] [utilities + primary action]
headerCompositions.selectWhen: Visitors need several discoverable routes into a broad offering.
headerCompositions.tradeoff: A dense left cluster competes with the page and reaches its compact breakpoint earlier.

headerCompositions.selectWhen: A focused offer or campaign supports a small immediate decision set.
headerCompositions.tradeoff: Secondary routes need another discoverable access point; reducing navigation must not conceal necessary information.

headerCompositions.structure: [equal flexible side track: identity] [destinations] [equal flexible side track: actions]
headerCompositions.selectWhen: A compact destination set benefits from a balanced independent center.
headerCompositions.tradeoff: Long labels or asymmetric side groups require earlier adaptation; space-between is not true centering.

headerCompositions.structure: [Identity + categorized destination menus] [flexible space] [search/account/actions as needed]
headerCompositions.selectWhen: A deeper information architecture warrants meaningful categories.
headerCompositions.tradeoff: Disclosures add interaction and require clear category boundaries, focus behavior and dismissal.

headerRules: Separate identity, destinations and utilities/actions into explicit regions.
Use smaller foundation gaps within groups and larger gaps between groups; align control centers on a shared row.
For true centering use equal flexible side columns, not space-between with unequal side widths.
Constrain the inner header with the same content alignment strategy as the page; its background remains full width.
Adapt before groups collide, considering real labels, localization, zoom and available width. Preserve destination hierarchy and keyboard access.
Information architecture (direct links, dropdowns, mega menu) is independent from header composition. Choose each for audience and content needs.
Do not invent search, account access or product actions to fill a reference layout. Omit unsupported responsibilities.
Distinguish configurable alignment from substantive A/B/C hypotheses. Use rationales tied to discovery, readiness and tradeoffs.
labelRules: Prefer one familiar word; use at most three short words when needed for recognition.
Author destination labels separately from descriptive page titles; preserve route IDs and never mechanically truncate.
Keep destination vocabulary consistent across responsive and local navigation.
alignmentRules: Navigation and section content share one content width cap and minimum gutter.
Backgrounds and section borders fill the wrapper; narrower reading measures nest inside the shared grid.
Balance identity, destinations and trailing utilities; use a relevant public CTA or signed-in user menu, and collapse before collision.
